skill.displayName: Workplace Group Stress Heatmap | 职场员工压力群体热力图

version.changelog:

llm.summary: The skill has a clear workplace stress heatmap purpose, but it handles sensitive employee-camera footage with unsafe default HTTP endpoints and persists cloud tokens locally without adequate disclosure or protection.

dimensions.detail: For highly sensitive workplace video, the default dev configuration routes health and analysis API traffic to plaintext HTTP private-network endpoints, and the request layer attaches authentication headers without enforcing HTTPS.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package uses normal Python scripts and pinned/common dependencies, but the distributed configuration selects a development environment by default.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions require automatic cloud history queries and hidden internal identity handling, with little user control over when identity-backed history is accessed or how remote processing is scoped.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The code creates a workspace data directory and SQLite database, generates or reuses a default user identity, and stores token/open_token fields as ordinary database strings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is employee-camera group stress analysis with cloud report retrieval; video upload, remote polling, and report links fit that purpose, but the skill repeatedly promises anonymity while also silently creating/reusing an internal identity for report association.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. This skill processes employee surveillance footage and sends analysis data to cloud services; require employee notice/consent, confirm the backend endpoints are HTTPS production endpoints, rotate any exposed credentials, and avoid use until token storage and identity/report retention are clearly documented and protected.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: Accepted. The artifact confirms config.yaml sets env: dev, config-dev.yaml uses http:// endpoints, and RequestUtil attaches access tokens and Authorization headers before making requests.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted. The artifact confirms returned token and openToken values are saved into a SQLite-backed User model with token/open_token string columns.
[TP4] unexpected: Partially accepted. Remote API analysis is purpose-aligned, but silent identity creation, local persistence, and token-backed report association materially weaken the skill's anonymity framing.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted as a disclosure concern. The skill mentions consent and anonymity, but not prominently enough for camera-based employee stress inference and cloud processing.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted. The code resolves or creates persistent default identities and stores authentication token fields locally, which is broader than anonymous group-only analysis.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in part. Generic authentication, user provisioning, billing messaging, and cloud history support are present; some cloud integration is expected, but the identity and credential handling is under-scoped for this sensitive use case.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted as a contributing concern because the skill needs file, shell, and network capabilities for sensitive video analysis but does not provide a narrow permissions boundary in the artifact.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded. Chinese and bilingual strings are hardcoded, but this is a usability/localization issue rather than a security reason for the verdict.
[P9] expected: Downgraded. The whitespace flagged in the inspected file appears to be ordinary line-wrapping indentation, with no hidden prompt-injection content found.
